figures.question: Does the derived fourth-order coefficient explain the inspected residual sign and scaling?
figures.reading: Compare the saved Test 7 amplitude ladder at the same nominal A=.004 marker times.
figures.significance: This diagnoses the missing order independently of a fitted coefficient.
figures.limitation: The prior histories and marker times were already inspected; this is not a prospective prediction.
transformations: formal Taylor coefficient times A^4; fixed nominal A=.004 markers from old receiver

figures.question: Does the locked fourth-order prediction improve a new local clock history?
figures.reading: Held-out finest trace error: second 0.1882%, fourth 0.1712%.
figures.significance: A separate waveform tests the coefficient after the inspected-history diagnostic.
figures.limitation: Quiet phase at the pulse markers is counterfactual; grid differences and inversion error remain.
transformations: matched quiet subtraction; exact quadrature Taylor expansion; no fit

figures.question: Do derivative-informed markers and twice-frequent output explain local timing error?
figures.reading: On h=.025, compare markers at 0.05 and decimated 0.1; coarse vacuum/known-Z maximum errors are 0.05998/0.05981.
figures.significance: Separates temporal interpolation from surface-propagation error.
figures.limitation: The coarse vacuum control is post-hoc; Hermite cannot repair spatial dispersion or WKB error.
transformations: linear threshold crossings; cubic Hermite with local a_t; decimate .05 to .1
